content.english: Jas 1:12

segments.t: Iac 1:12

content.latin: Beátus vir, qui suffert tentatiónem: quóniam cum probátus fúerit, accípiet corónam vitæ, quam repromísit Deus diligéntibus se.
content.english: Blessed is the man that endureth temptation; for when he hath been proved, he shall receive a crown of life, which God hath promised to them that love him.

content.latin: ℟. Deo grátias.
content.english: ℟. Thanks be to God.

segments.t: Deo grátias.

content.latin: Hymnus
content.english: Hymn

segments.t: Hymnus

content.latin: Invícte Martyr, únicum
content.english: Martyr of God, whose strength was steeled

content.latin: Patris secútus Fílium,
content.english: To follow close God's only Son,

content.latin: Victis triúmphas hóstibus,
content.english: Well didst thou brave thy battlefield,

content.latin: Victor fruens cæléstibus.
content.english: And well thy heavenly bliss was won!

content.latin: Tui precátus múnere
content.english: Now join thy prayers with ours, who pray

content.latin: Nostrum reátum dílue,
content.english: That God may pardon us and bless;

content.latin: Arcens mali contágium,
content.english: For prayer keeps evil's plague away,

content.latin: Vitæ repéllens tǽdium.
content.english: And draws from life its weariness.

content.latin: Solúta sunt iam víncula
content.english: Long, long ago, were loosed the chains

content.latin: Tui sacráti córporis:
content.english: That held thy body once in thrall;

content.latin: Nos solve vinclis sǽculi,
content.english: For us how many a bond remains!

content.latin: Dono supérni Núminis.
content.english: O love of God release us all.

content.latin: Deo Patri sit glória,
content.english: All praise to God the Father be,

content.latin: Eiúsque soli Fílio,
content.english: All praise to thee, Eternal Son;

content.latin: Cum Spíritu Paráclito,
content.english: All praise, O Holy Ghost, to thee,

content.latin: Nunc, et per omne sǽculum.
content.english: While never-ending ages run.

content.latin: Amen.
content.english: Amen.

content.latin: ℣. Iustus ut palma florébit.
content.english: ℣. The righteous shall flourish like the palm-tree.

segments.t: Iustus ut palma florébit.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut cedrus Líbani multiplicábitur.
content.english: ℟. He shall grow like a cedar in Lebanon.

segments.t: Sicut cedrus Líbani multiplicábitur.

content.latin: Ant. Qui odit * ánimam suam in hoc mundo, in vitam ætérnam custódit eam.
content.english: Ant. He that hateth his life * in this world, shall keep it unto life eternal.

segments.t: Ant.
Qui odit * ánimam suam in hoc mundo, in vitam ætérnam custódit eam.

content.latin: Canticum Zachariæ
content.english: Canticle of Zacharias

segments.t: Canticum Zachariæ

content.latin: 1:68 Benedíctus ✠ Dóminus, Deus Israël: * quia visitávit, et fecit redemptiónem plebis suæ:
content.english: 1:68 Blessed be the Lord ✠ God of Israel; * because he hath visited and wrought the redemption of his people:

segments.t: Benedíctus ✠ Dóminus, Deus Israël: * quia visitávit, et fecit redemptiónem plebis suæ:

content.latin: 1:69 Et eréxit cornu salútis nobis: * in domo David, púeri sui.
content.english: 1:69 And hath raised up an horn of salvation to us, * in the house of David his servant:

segments.t: Et eréxit cornu salútis nobis: * in domo David, púeri sui.

content.latin: 1:70 Sicut locútus est per os sanctórum, * qui a sǽculo sunt, prophetárum eius:
content.english: 1:70 As he spoke by the mouth of his holy Prophets, * who are from the beginning:

segments.t: Sicut locútus est per os sanctórum, * qui a sǽculo sunt, prophetárum eius:

content.latin: 1:71 Salútem ex inimícis nostris, * et de manu ómnium, qui odérunt nos.
content.english: 1:71 Salvation from our enemies, * and from the hand of all that hate us:

segments.t: Salútem ex inimícis nostris, * et de manu ómnium, qui odérunt nos.

content.latin: 1:72 Ad faciéndam misericórdiam cum pátribus nostris: * et memorári testaménti sui sancti.
content.english: 1:72 To perform mercy to our fathers, * and to remember his holy testament,

segments.t: Ad faciéndam misericórdiam cum pátribus nostris: * et memorári testaménti sui sancti.

content.latin: 1:73 Iusiurándum, quod iurávit ad Ábraham patrem nostrum, * datúrum se nobis:
content.english: 1:73 The oath, which he swore to Abraham our father, * that he would grant to us,

segments.t: Iusiurándum, quod iurávit ad Ábraham patrem nostrum, * datúrum se nobis:

content.latin: 1:74 Ut sine timóre, de manu inimicórum nostrórum liberáti, * serviámus illi.
content.english: 1:74 That being delivered from the hand of our enemies, * we may serve him without fear,

segments.t: Ut sine timóre, de manu inimicórum nostrórum liberáti, * serviámus illi.

content.latin: 1:75 In sanctitáte, et iustítia coram ipso, * ómnibus diébus nostris.
content.english: 1:75 In holiness and justice before him, * all our days.

segments.t: In sanctitáte, et iustítia coram ipso, * ómnibus diébus nostris.

content.latin: 1:76 Et tu, puer, Prophéta Altíssimi vocáberis: * præíbis enim ante fáciem Dómini, paráre vias eius:
content.english: 1:76 And thou, child, shalt be called the prophet of the Highest: * for thou shalt go before the face of the Lord to prepare his ways:

segments.t: Et tu, puer, Prophéta Altíssimi vocáberis: * præíbis enim ante fáciem Dómini, paráre vias eius:

content.latin: 1:77 Ad dandam sciéntiam salútis plebi eius: * in remissiónem peccatórum eórum:
content.english: 1:77 To give knowledge of salvation to his people, * unto the remission of their sins:

segments.t: Ad dandam sciéntiam salútis plebi eius: * in remissiónem peccatórum eórum:

content.latin: 1:78 Per víscera misericórdiæ Dei nostri: * in quibus visitávit nos, óriens ex alto:
content.english: 1:78 Through the bowels of the mercy of our God, * in which the Orient from on high hath visited us:

segments.t: Per víscera misericórdiæ Dei nostri: * in quibus visitávit nos, óriens ex alto:

content.latin: 1:79 Illumináre his, qui in ténebris, et in umbra mortis sedent: * ad dirigéndos pedes nostros in viam pacis.
content.english: 1:79 To enlighten them that sit in darkness, and in the shadow of death: * to direct our feet into the way of peace.

content.latin: Excita, quǽsumus, Dómine, in Ecclésia tua Spíritum, quo replétus beátus Iósaphat Martyr et Póntifex tuus ánimam suam pro óvibus pósuit: ut, eo intercedénte, nos quoque eódem Spíritu moti ac roboráti, ánimam nostram pro frátribus pónere non vereámur.
content.english: Stir up in thy Church, we beseech thee, O Lord, that Spirit which so filled blessed Josaphat, thy Martyr and Bishop, that he laid down his life for his flock; that by his intercession we, being likewise animated and strengthened by that same Spirit, may not fear to lay down our lives for our brethren.

content.english: Lowly of heart, our God we pray

content.latin: Ut in diúrnis áctibus
content.english: That he from harm may keep us free

content.english: In all the deeds this day shall see.

content.english: May fear of him our tongues restrain,

content.english: May every heart be pure from sin

content.latin: Absístat et vecórdia;
content.english: And folly find no place therein:

content.latin: Carnis terat supérbiam
content.english: Scant need of food, excess denied,

content.latin: Potus cibíque párcitas.
content.english: Wear down in us the body's pride.

content.latin: Ut, cum dies abscésserit,
content.english: That when the light of day is gone,

content.latin: Noctémque sors redúxerit,
content.english: And night in course shall follow on.

content.latin: Mundi per abstinéntiam
content.english: We, free from cares the world affords,

content.latin: 93:1 Deus ultiónum Dóminus: * Deus ultiónum líbere egit.
content.english: 93:1 The Lord is the God to whom revenge belongeth: * the God of revenge hath acted freely.

segments.t: Deus ultiónum Dóminus: * Deus ultiónum líbere egit.

content.latin: 93:2 Exaltáre, qui iúdicas terram: * redde retributiónem supérbis.
content.english: 93:2 Lift up thyself, thou that judgest the earth: * render a reward to the proud.

segments.t: Exaltáre, qui iúdicas terram: * redde retributiónem supérbis.

content.latin: 93:3 Úsquequo peccatóres, Dómine, * úsquequo peccatóres gloriabúntur:
content.english: 93:3 How long shall sinners, O Lord: * how long shall sinners glory?

segments.t: Úsquequo peccatóres, Dómine, * úsquequo peccatóres gloriabúntur:

content.latin: 93:4 Effabúntur, et loquéntur iniquitátem: * loquéntur omnes, qui operántur iniustítiam?
content.english: 93:4 Shall they utter, and speak iniquity: * shall all speak who work injustice?

segments.t: Effabúntur, et loquéntur iniquitátem: * loquéntur omnes, qui operántur iniustítiam?

content.latin: 93:5 Pópulum tuum, Dómine, humiliavérunt: * et hereditátem tuam vexavérunt.
content.english: 93:5 Thy people, O Lord, they have brought low: * and they have afflicted thy inheritance.

segments.t: Pópulum tuum, Dómine, humiliavérunt: * et hereditátem tuam vexavérunt.

content.latin: 93:6 Víduam, et ádvenam interfecérunt: * et pupíllos occidérunt.
content.english: 93:6 They have slain the widow and the stranger: * and they have murdered the fatherless.

segments.t: Víduam, et ádvenam interfecérunt: * et pupíllos occidérunt.

content.latin: 93:7 Et dixérunt: Non vidébit Dóminus, * nec intélleget Deus Iacob.
content.english: 93:7 And they have said: The Lord shall not see: * neither shall the God of Jacob understand.

segments.t: Et dixérunt: Non vidébit Dóminus, * nec intélleget Deus Iacob.

content.latin: 93:8 Intellégite, insipiéntes in pópulo: * et stulti, aliquándo sápite.
content.english: 93:8 Understand, ye senseless among the people: * and, you fools, be wise at last.

segments.t: Intellégite, insipiéntes in pópulo: * et stulti, aliquándo sápite.

content.latin: 93:9 Qui plantávit aurem, non áudiet? * aut qui finxit óculum, non consíderat?
content.english: 93:9 He that planted the ear, shall he not hear? * or he that formed the eye, doth he not consider?

segments.t: Qui plantávit aurem, non áudiet? * aut qui finxit óculum, non consíderat?

content.latin: 93:10 Qui córripit gentes, non árguet: * qui docet hóminem sciéntiam?
content.english: 93:10 He that chastiseth nations, shall he not rebuke: * he that teacheth man knowledge?

segments.t: Qui córripit gentes, non árguet: * qui docet hóminem sciéntiam?

content.latin: 93:11 Dóminus scit cogitatiónes hóminum, * quóniam vanæ sunt.
content.english: 93:11 The Lord knoweth the thoughts of men, * that they are vain.

segments.t: Dóminus scit cogitatiónes hóminum, * quóniam vanæ sunt.

content.latin: 93:12 Beátus homo, quem tu erudíeris, Dómine: * et de lege tua docúeris eum,
content.english: 93:12 Blessed is the man whom thou shalt instruct, O Lord: * and shalt teach him out of thy law.

segments.t: Beátus homo, quem tu erudíeris, Dómine: * et de lege tua docúeris eum,

content.latin: 93:13 Ut mítiges ei a diébus malis: * donec fodiátur peccatóri fóvea.
content.english: 93:13 That thou mayst give him rest from the evil days: * till a pit be dug for the wicked.

segments.t: Ut mítiges ei a diébus malis: * donec fodiátur peccatóri fóvea.

content.latin: 93:14 Quia non repéllet Dóminus plebem suam: * et hereditátem suam non derelínquet.
content.english: 93:14 For the Lord will not cast off his people: * neither will he forsake his own inheritance.

segments.t: Quia non repéllet Dóminus plebem suam: * et hereditátem suam non derelínquet.

content.latin: 93:15 Quoadúsque iustítia convertátur in iudícium: * et qui iuxta illam omnes qui recto sunt corde.
content.english: 93:15 Until justice be turned into judgment: * and they that are near it are all the upright in heart.

segments.t: Quoadúsque iustítia convertátur in iudícium: * et qui iuxta illam omnes qui recto sunt corde.

content.latin: 93:16 Quis consúrget mihi advérsus malignántes? * aut quis stabit mecum advérsus operántes iniquitátem?
content.english: 93:16 Who shall rise up for me against the evildoers? * or who shall stand with me against the workers of iniquity?

segments.t: Quis consúrget mihi advérsus malignántes? * aut quis stabit mecum advérsus operántes iniquitátem?

content.latin: 93:17 Nisi quia Dóminus adiúvit me: * paulo minus habitásset in inférno ánima mea.
content.english: 93:17 Unless the Lord had been my helper, * my soul had almost dwelt in hell.

segments.t: Nisi quia Dóminus adiúvit me: * paulo minus habitásset in inférno ánima mea.

content.latin: 93:18 Si dicébam: Motus est pes meus: * misericórdia tua, Dómine, adiuvábat me.
content.english: 93:18 If I said: My foot is moved: * thy mercy, O Lord, assisted me.

segments.t: Si dicébam: Motus est pes meus: * misericórdia tua, Dómine, adiuvábat me.

content.latin: 93:19 Secúndum multitúdinem dolórum meórum in corde meo: * consolatiónes tuæ lætificavérunt ánimam meam.
content.english: 93:19 According to the multitude of my sorrows in my heart, * thy comforts have given joy to my soul.

segments.t: Secúndum multitúdinem dolórum meórum in corde meo: * consolatiónes tuæ lætificavérunt ánimam meam.

content.latin: 93:20 Numquid adhǽret tibi sedes iniquitátis: * qui fingis labórem in præcépto?
content.english: 93:20 Doth the seat of iniquity stick to thee, * who framest labour in commandment?

segments.t: Numquid adhǽret tibi sedes iniquitátis: * qui fingis labórem in præcépto?

content.latin: 93:21 Captábunt in ánimam iusti: * et sánguinem innocéntem condemnábunt.
content.english: 93:21 They will hunt after the soul of the just, * and will condemn innocent blood.

segments.t: Captábunt in ánimam iusti: * et sánguinem innocéntem condemnábunt.

content.latin: 93:22 Et factus est mihi Dóminus in refúgium: * et Deus meus in adiutórium spei meæ.
content.english: 93:22 But the Lord is my refuge: * and my God the help of my hope.

segments.t: Et factus est mihi Dóminus in refúgium: * et Deus meus in adiutórium spei meæ.

content.latin: 93:23 Et reddet illis iniquitátem ipsórum: et in malítia eórum dispérdet eos: * dispérdet illos Dóminus, Deus noster.
content.english: 93:23 And he will render them their iniquity: and in their malice he will destroy them: * the Lord our God will destroy them.

segments.t: Et reddet illis iniquitátem ipsórum: et in malítia eórum dispérdet eos: * dispérdet illos Dóminus, Deus noster.

content.latin: 107:2 Parátum cor meum, Deus, parátum cor meum: * cantábo, et psallam in glória mea.
content.english: 107:2 My heart is ready, O God, my heart is ready: * I will sing, and will give praise, with my glory.

segments.t: Parátum cor meum, Deus, parátum cor meum: * cantábo, et psallam in glória mea.

content.latin: 107:3 Exsúrge, glória mea, exsúrge, psaltérium et cíthara: * exsúrgam dilúculo.
content.english: 107:3 Arise, my glory; arise, psaltery and harp * I will arise in the morning early.

segments.t: Exsúrge, glória mea, exsúrge, psaltérium et cíthara: * exsúrgam dilúculo.

content.latin: 107:4 Confitébor tibi in pópulis, Dómine: * et psallam tibi in natiónibus.
content.english: 107:4 I will praise thee, O Lord, among the people: * and I will sing unto thee among the nations.

segments.t: Confitébor tibi in pópulis, Dómine: * et psallam tibi in natiónibus.

content.latin: 107:5 Quia magna est super cælos misericórdia tua: * et usque ad nubes véritas tua:
content.english: 107:5 For thy mercy is great above the heavens: * and thy truth even unto the clouds.

segments.t: Quia magna est super cælos misericórdia tua: * et usque ad nubes véritas tua:

content.latin: 107:6 Exaltáre super cælos, Deus, et super omnem terram glória tua: * ut liberéntur dilécti tui.
content.english: 107:6 Be thou exalted, O God, above the heavens, and thy glory over all the earth: * that thy beloved may be delivered.

segments.t: Exaltáre super cælos, Deus, et super omnem terram glória tua: * ut liberéntur dilécti tui.

content.latin: 107:7 Salvum fac déxtera tua, et exáudi me: * Deus locútus est in sancto suo:
content.english: 107:7 Save with thy right hand and hear me. * God hath spoken in his holiness.

segments.t: Salvum fac déxtera tua, et exáudi me: * Deus locútus est in sancto suo:

content.latin: 107:8 Exsultábo, et dívidam Síchimam, * et convállem tabernaculórum dimétiar.
content.english: 107:8 I will rejoice, and I will divide Sichem * and I will mete out the vale of tabernacles.

segments.t: Exsultábo, et dívidam Síchimam, * et convállem tabernaculórum dimétiar.

content.latin: 107:9 Meus est Gálaad, et meus est Manásses: * et Éphraim suscéptio cápitis mei.
content.english: 107:9 Galaad is mine: and Manasses is mine: * and Ephraim the protection of my head.

segments.t: Meus est Gálaad, et meus est Manásses: * et Éphraim suscéptio cápitis mei.

content.latin: 107:10 Iuda rex meus: * Moab lebes spei meæ.
content.english: 107:10 Juda is my king: * Moab the pot of my hope.

segments.t: Iuda rex meus: * Moab lebes spei meæ.

content.latin: 107:10 In Idumǽam exténdam calceaméntum meum: * mihi alienígenæ amíci facti sunt.
content.english: 107:10 Over Edom I will stretch out my shoe: * the aliens are become my friends.

segments.t: In Idumǽam exténdam calceaméntum meum: * mihi alienígenæ amíci facti sunt.

content.latin: 107:11 Quis dedúcet me in civitátem munítam? * quis dedúcet me usque in Idumǽam?
content.english: 107:11 Who will bring me into the strong city? * who will lead me into Edom?

segments.t: Quis dedúcet me in civitátem munítam? * quis dedúcet me usque in Idumǽam?

content.latin: 107:12 Nonne tu, Deus, qui repulísti nos, * et non exíbis, Deus, in virtútibus nostris?
content.english: 107:12 Wilt not thou, O God, who hast cast us off? * and wilt not thou, O God, go forth with our armies?

segments.t: Nonne tu, Deus, qui repulísti nos, * et non exíbis, Deus, in virtútibus nostris?

content.latin: 107:13 Da nobis auxílium de tribulatióne: * quia vana salus hóminis.
content.english: 107:13 O grant us help from trouble: * for vain is the help of man.

segments.t: Da nobis auxílium de tribulatióne: * quia vana salus hóminis.

content.latin: 107:14 In Deo faciémus virtútem: * et ipse ad níhilum dedúcet inimícos nostros.
content.english: 107:14 Through God we shall do mightily: * and he will bring our enemies to nothing.

segments.t: In Deo faciémus virtútem: * et ipse ad níhilum dedúcet inimícos nostros.

content.latin: Dómine Deus omnípotens, qui ad princípium huius diéi nos perveníre fecísti: tua nos hódie salva virtúte; ut in hac die ad nullum declinémus peccátum, sed semper ad tuam iustítiam faciéndam nostra procédant elóquia, dirigántur cogitatiónes et ópera.

content.english: The holy martyr Eugene, Archbishop of Toledo, a disciple of blessed Denys, the Areopagite. He finished his testimony in the country of Paris, and received from the Lord a blessed crown of suffering, (in the year 95.) His body was afterwards brought to Toledo.

content.latin: Nolæ, in Campánia, beáti Felícis, Epíscopi et Mártyris; qui, a quintodécimo ætátis suæ anno, miráculis cláruit, et, sub Marciáno Prǽside, cum áliis trigínta Sóciis, agónem martýrii complévit.
content.english: At Nola, in Campania, the holy martyr Felix, Bishop (of that see,) who was famous for miracles from the fifteenth year of his age upward and gained the battle of martyrdom under the President Marcian, along with thirty others.

content.latin: Edéssæ, in Mesopotámia, pássio sancti Abibi Diáconi, qui sub Licínio Imperatóre et Lysánia Prǽside, únguibus lacerátus, in ignem coniéctus est.
content.english: At Edessa, in Syria, under the Emperor Diocletian and Antonine the President, the holy martyrs Gurias and Samonas.

content.latin: Ibídem sanctórum Mártyrum Guríæ et Samónæ, sub Diocletiáno Imperatóre et Antoníno Prǽside.
content.english: There likewise, under the Emperor Licinius and the President Lysanias, the holy Deacon Abibus, who was torn with hooks and cast into the fire.

content.latin: In Africa sanctórum Mártyrum Secúndi, Fidentiáni et Várici.
content.english: In Africa, the holy martyrs Secundus, Fidentian, and Varicus.

content.latin: Apud Arcum, in território Santonénsi, natális sancti Machúti, Aleténsis in Gállia Epíscopi; qui, in Anglia natus, a primǽvo ætátis suæ tirocínio miráculis emícuit.
content.english: In Brittany, (in the sixth century,) holy Machutus, (St. Maclou or St. Malo, first) Bishop (of the ancient See of Aleth, in Brittany,) who was marked by miracles even from his youth upward.

content.latin: Verónæ sancti Lupérii, Epíscopi et Confessóris.

content.latin: 101:2 Dómine, exáudi oratiónem meam: * et clamor meus ad te véniat.
content.english: 101:2 Hear, O Lord, my prayer: * and let my cry come to thee.

segments.t: Dómine, exáudi oratiónem meam: * et clamor meus ad te véniat.

content.latin: 101:3 Non avértas fáciem tuam a me: * in quacúmque die tríbulor, inclína ad me aurem tuam.
content.english: 101:3 Turn not away thy face from me: * in the day when I am in trouble, incline thy ear to me.

segments.t: Non avértas fáciem tuam a me: * in quacúmque die tríbulor, inclína ad me aurem tuam.

content.latin: 101:3 In quacúmque die invocávero te, * velóciter exáudi me.
content.english: 101:3 In what day soever I shall call upon thee, * hear me speedily.

segments.t: In quacúmque die invocávero te, * velóciter exáudi me.

content.latin: 101:4 Quia defecérunt sicut fumus dies mei: * et ossa mea sicut crémium aruérunt.
content.english: 101:4 For my days are vanished like smoke: * and my bones are grown dry like fuel for the fire.

segments.t: Quia defecérunt sicut fumus dies mei: * et ossa mea sicut crémium aruérunt.

content.latin: 101:5 Percússus sum ut fænum, et áruit cor meum: * quia oblítus sum comédere panem meum.
content.english: 101:5 I am smitten as grass, and my heart is withered: * because I forgot to eat my bread.

segments.t: Percússus sum ut fænum, et áruit cor meum: * quia oblítus sum comédere panem meum.

content.latin: 101:6 A voce gémitus mei * adhǽsit os meum carni meæ.
content.english: 101:6 Through the voice of my groaning, * my bone hath cleaved to my flesh.

segments.t: A voce gémitus mei * adhǽsit os meum carni meæ.

content.latin: 101:7 Símilis factus sum pellicáno solitúdinis: * factus sum sicut nyctícorax in domicílio.
content.english: 101:7 I am become like to a pelican of the wilderness: * I am like a night raven in the house.

segments.t: Símilis factus sum pellicáno solitúdinis: * factus sum sicut nyctícorax in domicílio.

content.latin: 101:8 Vigilávi, * et factus sum sicut passer solitárius in tecto.
content.english: 101:8 I have watched, * and am become as a sparrow all alone on the housetop.

segments.t: Vigilávi, * et factus sum sicut passer solitárius in tecto.

content.latin: 101:9 Tota die exprobrábant mihi inimíci mei: * et qui laudábant me, advérsum me iurábant.

segments.t: Tota die exprobrábant mihi inimíci mei: * et qui laudábant me, advérsum me iurábant.

content.latin: 101:10 Quia cínerem tamquam panem manducábam, * et potum meum cum fletu miscébam.
content.english: 101:10 For I did eat ashes like bread, * and mingled my drink with weeping.

segments.t: Quia cínerem tamquam panem manducábam, * et potum meum cum fletu miscébam.

content.latin: 101:11 A fácie iræ et indignatiónis tuæ: * quia élevans allisísti me.
content.english: 101:11 Because of thy anger and indignation: * for having lifted me up thou hast thrown me down.

segments.t: A fácie iræ et indignatiónis tuæ: * quia élevans allisísti me.

content.latin: 101:12 Dies mei sicut umbra declinavérunt: * et ego sicut fænum árui.

segments.t: Dies mei sicut umbra declinavérunt: * et ego sicut fænum árui.

content.latin: 101:17 Quia ædificávit Dóminus Sion: * et vidébitur in glória sua.

segments.t: Ut annúntient in Sion nomen Dómini: * et laudem eius in Ierúsalem.

content.english: 101:23 When the people assemble together, * and kings, to serve the Lord.

Psalmus 101(24-29)

content.latin: 101:24 Respóndit ei in via virtútis suæ: * Paucitátem diérum meórum núntia mihi.
content.english: 101:24 He answered him in the way of his strength: * Declare unto me the fewness of my days.

segments.t: Respóndit ei in via virtútis suæ: * Paucitátem diérum meórum núntia mihi.

content.latin: 101:25 Ne révoces me in dimídio diérum meórum: * in generatiónem et generatiónem anni tui.
content.english: 101:25 Call me not away in the midst of my days: * thy years are unto generation and generation.

segments.t: Ne révoces me in dimídio diérum meórum: * in generatiónem et generatiónem anni tui.

content.latin: 101:26 Inítio tu, Dómine, terram fundásti: * et ópera mánuum tuárum sunt cæli.
content.english: 101:26 In the beginning, O Lord, thou foundedst the earth: * and the heavens are the works of thy hands.

segments.t: Inítio tu, Dómine, terram fundásti: * et ópera mánuum tuárum sunt cæli.

content.latin: 101:27 Ipsi períbunt, tu autem pérmanes: * et omnes sicut vestiméntum veteráscent.
content.english: 101:27 They shall perish but thou remainest: * and all of them shall grow old like a garment:

segments.t: Ipsi períbunt, tu autem pérmanes: * et omnes sicut vestiméntum veteráscent.

content.latin: 101:28 Et sicut opertórium mutábis eos, et mutabúntur: * tu autem idem ipse es, et anni tui non defícient.
content.english: 101:28 And as a vesture thou shalt change them, and they shall be changed. * But thou art always the selfsame, and thy years shall not fail.

segments.t: Et sicut opertórium mutábis eos, et mutabúntur: * tu autem idem ipse es, et anni tui non defícient.

content.latin: 101:29 Fílii servórum tuórum habitábunt: * et semen eórum in sǽculum dirigétur.
content.english: 101:29 The children of thy servants shall continue: * and their seed shall be directed for ever.

segments.t: Fílii servórum tuórum habitábunt: * et semen eórum in sǽculum dirigétur.

content.english: Jas 1:12

content.latin: Beátus vir, qui suffert tentatiónem: quóniam cum probátus fúerit, accípiet corónam vitæ, quam repromísit Deus diligéntibus se.
content.english: Blessed is the man that endureth temptation; for when he hath been proved, he shall receive a crown of life, which God hath promised to them that love him.

content.english: ℣. O Lord, Thou hast set a crown of precious stones.

content.english: ℟. Upon his head.

content.latin: Orémus.
content.english: Let us pray.

content.latin: Excita, quǽsumus, Dómine, in Ecclésia tua Spíritum, quo replétus beátus Iósaphat Martyr et Póntifex tuus ánimam suam pro óvibus pósuit: ut, eo intercedénte, nos quoque eódem Spíritu moti ac roboráti, ánimam nostram pro frátribus pónere non vereámur.
content.english: Stir up in thy Church, we beseech thee, O Lord, that Spirit which so filled blessed Josaphat, thy Martyr and Bishop, that he laid down his life for his flock; that by his intercession we, being likewise animated and strengthened by that same Spirit, may not fear to lay down our lives for our brethren.

content.latin: Per Dóminum nostrum Iesum Christum, Fílium tuum: qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitáte eiúsdem Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.
content.english: Through Jesus Christ, thy Son our Lord, Who liveth and reigneth with thee, in the unity of the same Holy Ghost, God, world without end.

content.english: ℟. Amen.

segments.t: Amen.

content.english: ℣. O Lord, hear my prayer.

content.english: ℟. And let my cry come unto thee.

content.english: ℣. Let us bless the Lord.

content.english: ℟. Thanks be to God.

content.english: ℣. May the souls of the faithful, through the mercy of God, rest in peace.

segments.t: Fidélium ánimæ per misericórdiam Dei requiéscant in pace.

content.english: ℣. O God, ✠ come to my assistance;

segments.t: Deus ✠ in adiutórium meum inténde.

content.english: ℟. O Lord, make haste to help me.

segments.t: Dómine, ad adiuvándum me festína.

content.latin: Allelúia.
content.english: Alleluia.

content.latin: Rector potens, verax Deus,
content.english: O God of truth, O Lord of might,

content.latin: Qui témperas rerum vices,
content.english: Who orderest time and change aright,

content.latin: Splendóre mane illúminas,
content.english: Who send’st the early morning ray,

content.latin: Et ígnibus merídiem:
content.english: And light’st the glow of perfect day:

content.latin: Exstíngue flammas lítium,
content.english: Extinguish thou each sinful fire,

content.latin: Aufer calórem nóxium,
content.english: And banish every ill desire;

content.latin: Confer salútem córporum,
content.english: And while thou keep’st the body whole,

content.latin: Verámque pacem córdium.
content.english: Shed forth thy peace upon the soul.

content.latin: Præsta, Pater piíssime,
content.english: Almighty Father, hear our cry,

content.latin: Patríque compar Únice,
content.english: Through Jesus Christ, our Lord most High,

content.latin: Cum Spíritu Paráclito
content.english: Who, with the Holy Ghost and thee,

content.latin: Regnans per omne sǽculum.
content.english: Doth live and reign eternally.

content.latin: Amen.
content.english: Amen.

content.latin: Ant. Dómine, Deus meus * magnificátus es veheménter.
content.english: Ant. O Lord, my God, * thou art exceedingly great.

segments.t: Ant.
Dómine, Deus meus * magnificátus es veheménter.
Psalmus 103(1-12)

content.latin: 103:1 Bénedic, ánima mea, Dómino: * Dómine, Deus meus, magnificátus es veheménter.
content.english: 103:1 Bless the Lord, O my soul: * O Lord my God, thou art exceedingly great.

segments.t: Bénedic, ánima mea, Dómino: * Dómine, Deus meus, magnificátus es veheménter.

content.latin: 103:1 Confessiónem, et decórem induísti: * amíctus lúmine sicut vestiménto:
content.english: 103:1 Thou hast put on praise and beauty: * and art clothed with light as with a garment.

segments.t: Confessiónem, et decórem induísti: * amíctus lúmine sicut vestiménto:

content.latin: 103:2 Exténdens cælum sicut pellem: * qui tegis aquis superióra eius.
content.english: 103:2 Who stretchest out the heaven like a pavilion: * who coverest the higher rooms thereof with water.

segments.t: Exténdens cælum sicut pellem: * qui tegis aquis superióra eius.

content.latin: 103:3 Qui ponis nubem ascénsum tuum: * qui ámbulas super pennas ventórum.
content.english: 103:3 Who makest the clouds thy chariot: * who walkest upon the wings of the winds.

segments.t: Qui ponis nubem ascénsum tuum: * qui ámbulas super pennas ventórum.

content.latin: 103:4 Qui facis ángelos tuos, spíritus: * et minístros tuos ignem uréntem.
content.english: 103:4 Who makest thy angels spirits: * and thy ministers a burning fire.

segments.t: Qui facis ángelos tuos, spíritus: * et minístros tuos ignem uréntem.

content.latin: 103:5 Qui fundásti terram super stabilitátem suam: * non inclinábitur in sǽculum sǽculi.
content.english: 103:5 Who hast founded the earth upon its own bases: * it shall not be moved for ever and ever.

segments.t: Qui fundásti terram super stabilitátem suam: * non inclinábitur in sǽculum sǽculi.

content.latin: 103:6 Abýssus, sicut vestiméntum, amíctus eius: * super montes stabunt aquæ.
content.english: 103:6 The deep like a garment is its clothing: * above the mountains shall the waters stand.

segments.t: Abýssus, sicut vestiméntum, amíctus eius: * super montes stabunt aquæ.

content.latin: 103:7 Ab increpatióne tua fúgient: * a voce tonítrui tui formidábunt.
content.english: 103:7 At thy rebuke they shall flee: * at the voice of thy thunder they shall fear.

segments.t: Ab increpatióne tua fúgient: * a voce tonítrui tui formidábunt.

content.latin: 103:8 Ascéndunt montes: et descéndunt campi * in locum, quem fundásti eis.
content.english: 103:8 The mountains ascend, and the plains descend * into the place which thou hast founded for them.

segments.t: Ascéndunt montes: et descéndunt campi * in locum, quem fundásti eis.

content.latin: 103:9 Términum posuísti, quem non transgrediéntur: * neque converténtur operíre terram.
content.english: 103:9 Thou hast set a bound which they shall not pass over; * neither shall they return to cover the earth.

segments.t: Términum posuísti, quem non transgrediéntur: * neque converténtur operíre terram.

content.latin: 103:10 Qui emíttis fontes in convállibus: * inter médium móntium pertransíbunt aquæ.
content.english: 103:10 Thou sendest forth springs in the vales: * between the midst of the hills the waters shall pass.

segments.t: Qui emíttis fontes in convállibus: * inter médium móntium pertransíbunt aquæ.

content.latin: 103:11 Potábunt omnes béstiæ agri: * exspectábunt ónagri in siti sua.
content.english: 103:11 All the beasts of the field shall drink: * the wild asses shall expect in their thirst.

segments.t: Potábunt omnes béstiæ agri: * exspectábunt ónagri in siti sua.

content.latin: 103:12 Super ea vólucres cæli habitábunt: * de médio petrárum dabunt voces.
content.english: 103:12 Over them the birds of the air shall dwell: * from the midst of the rocks they shall give forth their voices.

segments.t: Super ea vólucres cæli habitábunt: * de médio petrárum dabunt voces.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

segments.t: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

segments.t: Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
Psalmus 103(13-23)

content.latin: 103:13 Rigans montes de superióribus suis: * de fructu óperum tuórum satiábitur terra:
content.english: 103:13 Thou waterest the hills from thy upper rooms: * the earth shall be filled with the fruit of thy works:

segments.t: Rigans montes de superióribus suis: * de fructu óperum tuórum satiábitur terra:

content.latin: 103:14 Prodúcens fænum iuméntis, * et herbam servitúti hóminum:
content.english: 103:14 Bringing forth grass for cattle, * and herb for the service of men.

segments.t: Prodúcens fænum iuméntis, * et herbam servitúti hóminum:

content.latin: 103:14 Ut edúcas panem de terra: * et vinum lætíficet cor hóminis:
content.english: 103:14 That thou mayst bring bread out of the earth: * and that wine may cheer the heart of man.

segments.t: Ut edúcas panem de terra: * et vinum lætíficet cor hóminis:

content.latin: 103:15 Ut exhílaret fáciem in óleo: * et panis cor hóminis confírmet.
content.english: 103:15 That he may make the face cheerful with oil: * and that bread may strengthen man’s heart.

segments.t: Ut exhílaret fáciem in óleo: * et panis cor hóminis confírmet.

content.latin: 103:16 Saturabúntur ligna campi, et cedri Líbani, quas plantávit: * illic pásseres nidificábunt.
content.english: 103:16 The trees of the field shall be filled, and the cedars of Libanus which he hath planted: * there the sparrows shall make their nests.

segments.t: Saturabúntur ligna campi, et cedri Líbani, quas plantávit: * illic pásseres nidificábunt.

content.latin: 103:17 Heródii domus dux est eórum: * montes excélsi cervis: petra refúgium herináciis.
content.english: 103:17 The highest of them is the house of the heron. * The high hills are a refuge for the harts, the rock for the irchins.

segments.t: Heródii domus dux est eórum: * montes excélsi cervis: petra refúgium herináciis.

content.latin: 103:19 Fecit lunam in témpora: * sol cognóvit occásum suum.
content.english: 103:19 He hath made the moon for seasons: * the sun knoweth his going down.

segments.t: Fecit lunam in témpora: * sol cognóvit occásum suum.

content.latin: 103:20 Posuísti ténebras, et facta est nox: * in ipsa pertransíbunt omnes béstiæ silvæ.
content.english: 103:20 Thou hast appointed darkness, and it is night: * in it shall all the beasts of the woods go about:

segments.t: Posuísti ténebras, et facta est nox: * in ipsa pertransíbunt omnes béstiæ silvæ.

content.latin: 103:21 Cátuli leónum rugiéntes, ut rápiant, * et quærant a Deo escam sibi.
content.english: 103:21 The young lions roaring after their prey, * and seeking their meat from God.

segments.t: Cátuli leónum rugiéntes, ut rápiant, * et quærant a Deo escam sibi.

content.latin: 103:22 Ortus est sol, et congregáti sunt: * et in cubílibus suis collocabúntur.
content.english: 103:22 The sun ariseth, and they are gathered together: * and they shall lie down in their dens.

segments.t: Ortus est sol, et congregáti sunt: * et in cubílibus suis collocabúntur.

content.latin: 103:23 Exíbit homo ad opus suum: * et ad operatiónem suam usque ad vésperum.
content.english: 103:23 Man shall go forth to his work, * and to his labour until the evening.

segments.t: Exíbit homo ad opus suum: * et ad operatiónem suam usque ad vésperum.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

segments.t: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

segments.t: Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
Psalmus 103(24-35)

content.latin: 103:24 Quam magnificáta sunt ópera tua, Dómine! * ómnia in sapiéntia fecísti: impléta est terra possessióne tua.
content.english: 103:24 How great are thy works, O Lord? * thou hast made all things in wisdom: the earth is filled with thy riches.

segments.t: Quam magnificáta sunt ópera tua, Dómine! * ómnia in sapiéntia fecísti: impléta est terra possessióne tua.

content.latin: 103:25 Hoc mare magnum, et spatiósum mánibus: * illic reptília, quorum non est númerus.
content.english: 103:25 So is this great sea, which stretcheth wide its arms: * there are creeping things without number:

segments.t: Hoc mare magnum, et spatiósum mánibus: * illic reptília, quorum non est númerus.

content.latin: 103:26 Animália pusílla cum magnis: * illic naves pertransíbunt.
content.english: 103:26 Creatures little and great. * There the ships shall go.

segments.t: Animália pusílla cum magnis: * illic naves pertransíbunt.

content.latin: 103:27 Draco iste, quem formásti ad illudéndum ei: * ómnia a te exspéctant ut des illis escam in témpore.
content.english: 103:27 This sea dragon which thou hast formed to play therein. * All expect of thee that thou give them food in season.

segments.t: Draco iste, quem formásti ad illudéndum ei: * ómnia a te exspéctant ut des illis escam in témpore.

content.latin: 103:28 Dante te illis, cólligent: * aperiénte te manum tuam, ómnia implebúntur bonitáte.
content.english: 103:28 What thou givest to them they shall gather up: * when thou openest thy hand, they shall all be filled with good.

segments.t: Dante te illis, cólligent: * aperiénte te manum tuam, ómnia implebúntur bonitáte.

content.latin: 103:29 Averténte autem te fáciem, turbabúntur: * áuferes spíritum eórum, et defícient, et in púlverem suum reverténtur.
content.english: 103:29 But if thou turnest away thy face, they shall be troubled: * thou shalt take away their breath, and they shall fail, and shall return to their dust.

segments.t: Averténte autem te fáciem, turbabúntur: * áuferes spíritum eórum, et defícient, et in púlverem suum reverténtur.

content.latin: 103:30 Emíttes spíritum tuum, et creabúntur: * et renovábis fáciem terræ.
content.english: 103:30 Thou shalt send forth thy spirit, and they shall be created: * and thou shalt renew the face of the earth.

segments.t: Emíttes spíritum tuum, et creabúntur: * et renovábis fáciem terræ.

content.latin: 103:31 Sit glória Dómini in sǽculum: * lætábitur Dóminus in opéribus suis:
content.english: 103:31 May the glory of the Lord endure for ever: * the Lord shall rejoice in his works.

segments.t: Sit glória Dómini in sǽculum: * lætábitur Dóminus in opéribus suis:

content.latin: 103:32 Qui réspicit terram, et facit eam trémere: * qui tangit montes, et fúmigant.
content.english: 103:32 He looketh upon the earth, and maketh it tremble: * he toucheth the mountains, and they smoke.

segments.t: Qui réspicit terram, et facit eam trémere: * qui tangit montes, et fúmigant.

content.latin: 103:33 Cantábo Dómino in vita mea: * psallam Deo meo, quámdiu sum.
content.english: 103:33 I will sing to the Lord as long as I live: * I will sing praise to my God while I have my being.

segments.t: Cantábo Dómino in vita mea: * psallam Deo meo, quámdiu sum.

content.latin: 103:34 Iucúndum sit ei elóquium meum: * ego vero delectábor in Dómino.
content.english: 103:34 Let my speech be acceptable to him: * but I will take delight in the Lord.

segments.t: Iucúndum sit ei elóquium meum: * ego vero delectábor in Dómino.

Psalmus 108(2-13)

content.latin: 108:2 Deus, laudem meam ne tacúeris: * quia os peccatóris, et os dolósi super me apértum est.
content.english: 108:2 God, be not thou silent in my praise: * for the mouth of the wicked and the mouth of the deceitful man is opened against me.

segments.t: Deus, laudem meam ne tacúeris: * quia os peccatóris, et os dolósi super me apértum est.

content.latin: 108:3 Locúti sunt advérsum me lingua dolósa, et sermónibus ódii circumdedérunt me: * et expugnavérunt me gratis.
content.english: 108:3 They have spoken against me with deceitful tongues; and they have compassed me about with words of hatred; * and have fought against me without cause.

segments.t: Locúti sunt advérsum me lingua dolósa, et sermónibus ódii circumdedérunt me: * et expugnavérunt me gratis.

content.latin: 108:4 Pro eo ut me dilígerent, detrahébant mihi: * ego autem orábam.
content.english: 108:4 Instead of making me a return of love, they detracted me: * but I gave myself to prayer.

segments.t: Pro eo ut me dilígerent, detrahébant mihi: * ego autem orábam.

content.latin: 108:5 Et posuérunt advérsum me mala pro bonis: * et ódium pro dilectióne mea.
content.english: 108:5 And they repaid me evil for good: * and hatred for my love.

segments.t: Et posuérunt advérsum me mala pro bonis: * et ódium pro dilectióne mea.

content.latin: 108:6 Constítue super eum peccatórem: * et diábolus stet a dextris eius.
content.english: 108:6 Set thou the sinner over him: * and may the devil stand at his right hand.

segments.t: Constítue super eum peccatórem: * et diábolus stet a dextris eius.

content.latin: 108:7 Cum iudicátur, éxeat condemnátus: * et orátio eius fiat in peccátum.
content.english: 108:7 When he is judged, may he go out condemned; * and may his prayer be turned to sin.

segments.t: Cum iudicátur, éxeat condemnátus: * et orátio eius fiat in peccátum.

content.latin: 108:8 Fiant dies eius pauci: * et episcopátum eius accípiat alter.
content.english: 108:8 May his days be few: * and his bishopric let another take.

segments.t: Fiant dies eius pauci: * et episcopátum eius accípiat alter.

content.latin: 108:9 Fiant fílii eius órphani: * et uxor eius vídua.
content.english: 108:9 May his children be fatherless, * and his wife a widow.

segments.t: Fiant fílii eius órphani: * et uxor eius vídua.

content.latin: 108:10 Nutántes transferántur fílii eius, et mendícent: * et eiciántur de habitatiónibus suis.
content.english: 108:10 Let his children be carried about vagabonds, and beg; * and let them be cast out of their dwellings.

segments.t: Nutántes transferántur fílii eius, et mendícent: * et eiciántur de habitatiónibus suis.

content.latin: 108:11 Scrutétur fænerátor omnem substántiam eius: * et dirípiant aliéni labóres eius.
content.english: 108:11 May the usurer search all his substance: * and let strangers plunder his labours.

segments.t: Scrutétur fænerátor omnem substántiam eius: * et dirípiant aliéni labóres eius.

content.latin: 108:12 Non sit illi adiútor: * nec sit qui misereátur pupíllis eius.
content.english: 108:12 May there be none to help him: * nor none to pity his fatherless offspring.

segments.t: Non sit illi adiútor: * nec sit qui misereátur pupíllis eius.

content.latin: 108:13 Fiant nati eius in intéritum: * in generatióne una deleátur nomen eius.
content.english: 108:13 May his posterity be cut off; * in one generation may his name be blotted out.

segments.t: Fiant nati eius in intéritum: * in generatióne una deleátur nomen eius.

Psalmus 108(14-21)

content.latin: 108:14 In memóriam rédeat iníquitas patrum eius in conspéctu Dómini: * et peccátum matris eius non deleátur.
content.english: 108:14 May the iniquity of his fathers be remembered in the sight of the Lord: * and let not the sin of his mother be blotted out.

segments.t: In memóriam rédeat iníquitas patrum eius in conspéctu Dómini: * et peccátum matris eius non deleátur.

content.latin: 108:15 Fiant contra Dóminum semper, et dispéreat de terra memória eórum: * pro eo quod non est recordátus fácere misericórdiam.
content.english: 108:15 May they be before the Lord continually, and let the memory of them perish from the earth: * because he remembered not to shew mercy,

segments.t: Fiant contra Dóminum semper, et dispéreat de terra memória eórum: * pro eo quod non est recordátus fácere misericórdiam.

content.latin: 108:17 Et persecútus est hóminem ínopem, et mendícum, * et compúnctum corde mortificáre.
content.english: 108:17 But persecuted the poor man and the beggar; * and the broken in heart, to put him to death.

segments.t: Et persecútus est hóminem ínopem, et mendícum, * et compúnctum corde mortificáre.

content.latin: 108:18 Et diléxit maledictiónem, et véniet ei: * et nóluit benedictiónem, et elongábitur ab eo.
content.english: 108:18 And he loved cursing, and it shall come unto him: * and he would not have blessing, and it shall be far from him.

segments.t: Et diléxit maledictiónem, et véniet ei: * et nóluit benedictiónem, et elongábitur ab eo.

content.latin: 108:18 Et índuit maledictiónem sicut vestiméntum, * et intrávit sicut aqua in interióra eius, et sicut óleum in óssibus eius.
content.english: 108:18 And he put on cursing, like a garment: * and it went in like water into his entrails, and like oil in his bones.

segments.t: Et índuit maledictiónem sicut vestiméntum, * et intrávit sicut aqua in interióra eius, et sicut óleum in óssibus eius.

content.latin: 108:19 Fiat ei sicut vestiméntum, quo operítur: * et sicut zona, qua semper præcíngitur.
content.english: 108:19 May it be unto him like a garment which covereth him; * and like a girdle with which he is girded continually.

segments.t: Fiat ei sicut vestiméntum, quo operítur: * et sicut zona, qua semper præcíngitur.

content.latin: 108:20 Hoc opus eórum, qui détrahunt mihi apud Dóminum: * et qui loquúntur mala advérsus ánimam meam.
content.english: 108:20 This is the work of them who detract me before the Lord; * and who speak evils against my soul.

segments.t: Hoc opus eórum, qui détrahunt mihi apud Dóminum: * et qui loquúntur mala advérsus ánimam meam.

content.latin: 108:21 Et tu, Dómine, Dómine, fac mecum propter nomen tuum: * quia suávis est misericórdia tua.
content.english: 108:21 But thou, O Lord, do with me for thy name’s sake: * because thy mercy is sweet.

segments.t: Et tu, Dómine, Dómine, fac mecum propter nomen tuum: * quia suávis est misericórdia tua.

content.latin: 108:22 Líbera me quia egénus, et pauper ego sum: * et cor meum conturbátum est intra me.
content.english: 108:22 Do thou deliver me, for I am poor and needy, * and my heart is troubled within me.

segments.t: Líbera me quia egénus, et pauper ego sum: * et cor meum conturbátum est intra me.

content.latin: 108:23 Sicut umbra cum declínat, ablátus sum: * et excússus sum sicut locústæ.
content.english: 108:23 I am taken away like the shadow when it declineth: * and I am shaken off as locusts.

segments.t: Sicut umbra cum declínat, ablátus sum: * et excússus sum sicut locústæ.

content.latin: 108:24 Génua mea infirmáta sunt a ieiúnio: * et caro mea immutáta est propter óleum.
content.english: 108:24 My knees are weakened through fasting: * and my flesh is changed for oil.

segments.t: Génua mea infirmáta sunt a ieiúnio: * et caro mea immutáta est propter óleum.

content.latin: 108:25 Et ego factus sum oppróbrium illis: * vidérunt me, et movérunt cápita sua.
content.english: 108:25 And I am become a reproach to them: * they saw me and they shaked their heads.

segments.t: Et ego factus sum oppróbrium illis: * vidérunt me, et movérunt cápita sua.

content.latin: 108:26 Ádiuva me, Dómine, Deus meus: * salvum me fac secúndum misericórdiam tuam.
content.english: 108:26 Help me, O Lord my God; * save me according to thy mercy.

segments.t: Ádiuva me, Dómine, Deus meus: * salvum me fac secúndum misericórdiam tuam.

content.latin: 108:27 Et sciant quia manus tua hæc: * et tu, Dómine, fecísti eam.
content.english: 108:27 And let them know that this is thy hand: * and that thou, O Lord, hast done it.

segments.t: Et sciant quia manus tua hæc: * et tu, Dómine, fecísti eam.

content.latin: 108:28 Maledícent illi, et tu benedíces: * qui insúrgunt in me, confundántur: servus autem tuus lætábitur.
content.english: 108:28 They will curse and thou wilt bless: * let them that rise up against me be confounded: but thy servant shall rejoice.

segments.t: Maledícent illi, et tu benedíces: * qui insúrgunt in me, confundántur: servus autem tuus lætábitur.

content.latin: 108:29 Induántur qui détrahunt mihi, pudóre: * et operiántur sicut diplóide confusióne sua.
content.english: 108:29 Let them that detract me be clothed with shame: * and let them be covered with their confusion as with a double cloak.

segments.t: Induántur qui détrahunt mihi, pudóre: * et operiántur sicut diplóide confusióne sua.

content.latin: 108:30 Confitébor Dómino nimis in ore meo: * et in médio multórum laudábo eum.
content.english: 108:30 I will give great thanks to the Lord with my mouth: * and in the midst of many I will praise him.

segments.t: Confitébor Dómino nimis in ore meo: * et in médio multórum laudábo eum.

content.latin: 108:31 Quia ástitit a dextris páuperis, * ut salvam fáceret a persequéntibus ánimam meam.
content.english: 108:31 Because he hath stood at the right hand of the poor, * to save my soul from persecutors.

segments.t: Quia ástitit a dextris páuperis, * ut salvam fáceret a persequéntibus ánimam meam.

content.latin: Per Dóminum nostrum Iesum Christum, Fílium tuum: qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitáte eiúsdem Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.
content.english: Through Jesus Christ, thy Son our Lord, Who liveth and reigneth with thee, in the unity of the same Holy Ghost, God, world without end.

content.latin: 143:1 Benedíctus Dóminus, Deus meus, qui docet manus meas ad prǽlium, * et dígitos meos ad bellum.
content.english: 143:1 Blessed be the Lord my God, who teacheth my hands to fight, * and my fingers to war.

segments.t: Benedíctus Dóminus, Deus meus, qui docet manus meas ad prǽlium, * et dígitos meos ad bellum.

content.latin: 143:2 Misericórdia mea, et refúgium meum: * suscéptor meus, et liberátor meus:
content.english: 143:2 My mercy, and my refuge: * my support, and my deliverer:

segments.t: Misericórdia mea, et refúgium meum: * suscéptor meus, et liberátor meus:

content.latin: 143:2 Protéctor meus, et in ipso sperávi: * qui subdit pópulum meum sub me.
content.english: 143:2 My protector, and I have hoped in him: * who subdueth my people under me.

segments.t: Protéctor meus, et in ipso sperávi: * qui subdit pópulum meum sub me.

content.latin: 143:3 Dómine, quid est homo, quia innotuísti ei? * aut fílius hóminis, quia réputas eum?
content.english: 143:3 Lord, what is man, that thou art made known to him? * or the son of man, that thou makest account of him?

segments.t: Dómine, quid est homo, quia innotuísti ei? * aut fílius hóminis, quia réputas eum?

content.english: 143:4 Man is like to vanity: * his days pass away like a shadow.

segments.t: Homo vanitáti símilis factus est: * dies eius sicut umbra prætéreunt.

content.latin: 143:5 Dómine, inclína cælos tuos, et descénde: * tange montes, et fumigábunt.
content.english: 143:5 Lord, bow down thy heavens and descend: * touch the mountains, and they shall smoke.

segments.t: Dómine, inclína cælos tuos, et descénde: * tange montes, et fumigábunt.

segments.t: Fúlgura coruscatiónem, et dissipábis eos: * emítte sagíttas tuas, et conturbábis eos.

content.latin: 143:7 Emítte manum tuam de alto, éripe me, et líbera me de aquis multis: * de manu filiórum alienórum.

segments.t: Emítte manum tuam de alto, éripe me, et líbera me de aquis multis: * de manu filiórum alienórum.

content.latin: 143:8 Quorum os locútum est vanitátem: * et déxtera eórum, déxtera iniquitátis.
content.english: 143:8 Whose mouth hath spoken vanity: * and their right hand is the right hand of iniquity.

segments.t: Quorum os locútum est vanitátem: * et déxtera eórum, déxtera iniquitátis.

content.latin: 143:9 Deus, cánticum novum cantábo tibi: * in psaltério decachórdo psallam tibi.
content.english: 143:9 To thee, O God, I will sing a new canticle: * on the psaltery and an instrument of ten strings I will sing praises to thee.

segments.t: Deus, cánticum novum cantábo tibi: * in psaltério decachórdo psallam tibi.

content.latin: 143:10 Qui das salútem régibus: * qui redemísti David, servum tuum, de gládio malígno: éripe me.
content.english: 143:10 Who givest salvation to kings: * who hast redeemed thy servant David from the malicious sword: Deliver me,

content.latin: 143:11 Et érue me de manu filiórum alienórum, quorum os locútum est vanitátem: * et déxtera eórum, déxtera iniquitátis:
content.english: 143:11 And rescue me out of the hand of strange children; whose mouth hath spoken vanity: * and their right hand is the right hand of iniquity:

segments.t: Et érue me de manu filiórum alienórum, quorum os locútum est vanitátem: * et déxtera eórum, déxtera iniquitátis:

content.latin: 143:12 Quorum fílii, sicut novéllæ plantatiónes * in iuventúte sua.
content.english: 143:12 Whose sons are as new plants * in their youth:

segments.t: Quorum fílii, sicut novéllæ plantatiónes * in iuventúte sua.

content.latin: 143:12 Fíliæ eórum compósitæ: * circumornátæ ut similitúdo templi.
content.english: 143:12 Their daughters decked out, * adorned round about after the similitude of a temple:

segments.t: Fíliæ eórum compósitæ: * circumornátæ ut similitúdo templi.

content.latin: 143:13 Promptuária eórum plena, * eructántia ex hoc in illud.
content.english: 143:13 Their storehouses full, * flowing out of this into that.

segments.t: Promptuária eórum plena, * eructántia ex hoc in illud.

content.latin: 143:13 Oves eórum fœtósæ, abundántes in egréssibus suis: * boves eórum crassæ.
content.english: 143:13 Their sheep fruitful in young, abounding in their goings forth: * their oxen fat.

segments.t: Oves eórum fœtósæ, abundántes in egréssibus suis: * boves eórum crassæ.

content.latin: 143:14 Non est ruína macériæ, neque tránsitus: * neque clamor in platéis eórum.
content.english: 143:14 There is no breach of wall, nor passage, * nor crying out in their streets.

segments.t: Non est ruína macériæ, neque tránsitus: * neque clamor in platéis eórum.

content.latin: 143:15 Beátum dixérunt pópulum, cui hæc sunt: * beátus pópulus, cuius Dóminus Deus eius.
content.english: 143:15 They have called the people happy, that hath these things: * but happy is that people whose God is the Lord.

segments.t: Beátum dixérunt pópulum, cui hæc sunt: * beátus pópulus, cuius Dóminus Deus eius.

content.latin: 144:1 Exaltábo te, Deus meus, rex: * et benedícam nómini tuo in sǽculum, et in sǽculum sǽculi.
content.english: 144:1 I will extol thee, O God my king: * and I will bless thy name for ever; yea, for ever and ever.

segments.t: Exaltábo te, Deus meus, rex: * et benedícam nómini tuo in sǽculum, et in sǽculum sǽculi.

segments.t: Per síngulos dies benedícam tibi: * et laudábo nomen tuum in sǽculum, et in sǽculum sǽculi.

content.english: 144:3 Great is the Lord, and greatly to be praised: * and of his greatness there is no end.

segments.t: Magnus Dóminus, et laudábilis nimis: * et magnitúdinis eius non est finis.

content.latin: 144:4 Generátio et generátio laudábit ópera tua: * et poténtiam tuam pronuntiábunt.
content.english: 144:4 Generation and generation shall praise thy works: * and they shall declare thy power.

segments.t: Generátio et generátio laudábit ópera tua: * et poténtiam tuam pronuntiábunt.

content.latin: 144:5 Magnificéntiam glóriæ sanctitátis tuæ loquéntur: * et mirabília tua narrábunt.
content.english: 144:5 They shall speak of the magnificence of the glory of thy holiness: * and shall tell thy wondrous works.

segments.t: Magnificéntiam glóriæ sanctitátis tuæ loquéntur: * et mirabília tua narrábunt.

content.latin: 144:6 Et virtútem terribílium tuórum dicent: * et magnitúdinem tuam narrábunt.
content.english: 144:6 And they shall speak of the might of thy terrible acts: * and shall declare thy greatness.

segments.t: Et virtútem terribílium tuórum dicent: * et magnitúdinem tuam narrábunt.

content.latin: 144:7 Memóriam abundántiæ suavitátis tuæ eructábunt: * et iustítia tua exsultábunt.
content.english: 144:7 They shall publish the memory of the abundance of thy sweetness: * and shall rejoice in thy justice.

segments.t: Memóriam abundántiæ suavitátis tuæ eructábunt: * et iustítia tua exsultábunt.

segments.t: Iustus Dóminus in ómnibus viis suis: * et sanctus in ómnibus opéribus suis.

content.latin: Iam sol recédit ígneus:
content.english: As fades the glowing orb of day,

content.latin: Tu, lux perénnis, Únitas,
content.english: To thee, great source of light, we pray;

content.latin: Nostris, beáta Trínitas,
content.english: Blest Three in One, to every heart

content.latin: Infúnde lumen córdibus.
content.english: Thy beams of life and love impart.

content.latin: Te mane laudum cármine,
content.english: At early dawn, at close of day,

content.latin: Te deprecámur véspere;
content.english: To thee our vows we humbly pay;

content.latin: Dignéris ut te súpplices
content.english: May we, mid joys that never end,

content.latin: Laudémus inter cǽlites.
content.english: With thy bright saints in homage bend.

content.latin: Patri, simúlque Fílio,
content.english: To God the Father, and the Son,

content.latin: Tibíque, Sancte Spíritus,

content.latin: Pater noster, qui es in cælis, sanctificétur nomen tuum: advéniat regnum tuum: fiat volúntas tua, sicut in cælo et in terra. Panem nostrum cotidiánum da nobis hódie: et dimítte nobis débita nostra, sicut et nos dimíttimus debitóribus nostris: et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem: sed líbera nos a malo. Amen.
content.english: Our Father, who art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name. Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread. And forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us. And lead us not into temptation: But deliver us from evil. Amen.

content.latin: Confíteor Deo omnipoténti, beátæ Maríæ semper Vírgini, beáto Michaéli Archángelo, beáto Ioánni Baptístæ, sanctis Apóstolis Petro et Paulo, et ómnibus Sanctis, quia peccávi nimis, cogitatióne, verbo et ópere: percutit sibi pectus mea culpa, mea culpa, mea máxima culpa. Ídeo precor beátam Maríam semper Vírginem, beátum Michaélem Archángelum, beátum Ioánnem Baptístam, sanctos Apóstolos Petrum et Paulum, et omnes Sanctos, oráre pro me ad Dóminum Deum nostrum.
content.english: I confess to almighty God, to blessed Mary ever Virgin, to blessed Michael the Archangel, to blessed John the Baptist, to the holy Apostles Peter and Paul, and to all the Saints, that I have sinned exceedingly in thought, word and deed: strikes his breast through my fault, through my fault, through my most grievous fault. Therefore I beseech blessed Mary ever Virgin, blessed Michael the Archangel, blessed John the Baptist, the holy Apostles Peter and Paul, and all the Saints, to pray for me to the Lord our God.

segments.t: Confíteor Deo omnipoténti, beátæ Maríæ semper Vírgini, beáto Michaéli Archángelo, beáto Ioánni Baptístæ, sanctis Apóstolis Petro et Paulo, et ómnibus Sanctis, quia peccávi nimis, cogitatióne, verbo et ópere:

content.latin: 87:2 Dómine, Deus salútis meæ: * in die clamávi, et nocte coram te.
content.english: 87:2 Lord, the God of my salvation: * I have cried in the day, and in the night before thee.

segments.t: Dómine, Deus salútis meæ: * in die clamávi, et nocte coram te.

content.latin: 87:3 Intret in conspéctu tuo orátio mea: * inclína aurem tuam ad precem meam:
content.english: 87:3 Let my prayer come in before thee: * incline thy ear to my petition.

segments.t: Intret in conspéctu tuo orátio mea: * inclína aurem tuam ad precem meam:

content.latin: 87:4 Quia repléta est malis ánima mea: * et vita mea inférno appropinquávit.
content.english: 87:4 For my soul is filled with evils: * and my life hath drawn nigh to hell.

segments.t: Quia repléta est malis ánima mea: * et vita mea inférno appropinquávit.

content.latin: 87:5 Æstimátus sum cum descendéntibus in lacum: * factus sum sicut homo sine adiutório, inter mórtuos liber.
content.english: 87:5 I am counted among them that go down to the pit: * I am become as a man without help, free among the dead.

segments.t: Æstimátus sum cum descendéntibus in lacum: * factus sum sicut homo sine adiutório, inter mórtuos liber.

content.latin: 87:6 Sicut vulneráti dormiéntes in sepúlcris, quorum non es memor ámplius: * et ipsi de manu tua repúlsi sunt.
content.english: 87:6 Like the slain sleeping in the sepulchres, whom thou rememberest no more: * and they are cast off from thy hand.

segments.t: Sicut vulneráti dormiéntes in sepúlcris, quorum non es memor ámplius: * et ipsi de manu tua repúlsi sunt.

content.latin: 87:7 Posuérunt me in lacu inferióri: * in tenebrósis, et in umbra mortis.
content.english: 87:7 They have laid me in the lower pit: * in the dark places, and in the shadow of death.

segments.t: Posuérunt me in lacu inferióri: * in tenebrósis, et in umbra mortis.

content.latin: 87:8 Super me confirmátus est furor tuus: * et omnes fluctus tuos induxísti super me.
content.english: 87:8 Thy wrath is strong over me: * and all thy waves thou hast brought in upon me.

segments.t: Super me confirmátus est furor tuus: * et omnes fluctus tuos induxísti super me.

content.latin: 87:9 Longe fecísti notos meos a me: * posuérunt me abominatiónem sibi.
content.english: 87:9 Thou hast put away my acquaintance far from me: * they have set me an abomination to themselves.

segments.t: Longe fecísti notos meos a me: * posuérunt me abominatiónem sibi.

content.latin: 87:9 Tráditus sum, et non egrediébar: * óculi mei languérunt præ inópia.
content.english: 87:9 I was delivered up, and came not forth: * my eyes languished through poverty.

segments.t: Tráditus sum, et non egrediébar: * óculi mei languérunt præ inópia.

content.latin: 87:10 Clamávi ad te, Dómine, tota die: * expándi ad te manus meas.
content.english: 87:10 All the day I cried to thee, O Lord: * I stretched out my hands to thee.

segments.t: Clamávi ad te, Dómine, tota die: * expándi ad te manus meas.

content.latin: 87:11 Numquid mórtuis fácies mirabília: * aut médici suscitábunt, et confitebúntur tibi?
content.english: 87:11 Wilt thou shew wonders to the dead? * or shall physicians raise to life, and give praise to thee?

segments.t: Numquid mórtuis fácies mirabília: * aut médici suscitábunt, et confitebúntur tibi?

content.latin: 87:12 Numquid narrábit áliquis in sepúlcro misericórdiam tuam, * et veritátem tuam in perditióne?
content.english: 87:12 Shall any one in the sepulchre declare thy mercy: * and thy truth in destruction?

segments.t: Numquid narrábit áliquis in sepúlcro misericórdiam tuam, * et veritátem tuam in perditióne?

content.latin: 87:13 Numquid cognoscéntur in ténebris mirabília tua, * et iustítia tua in terra obliviónis?
content.english: 87:13 Shall thy wonders be known in the dark; * and thy justice in the land of forgetfulness?

segments.t: Numquid cognoscéntur in ténebris mirabília tua, * et iustítia tua in terra obliviónis?

content.latin: 87:14 Et ego ad te, Dómine, clamávi: * et mane orátio mea prævéniet te.
content.english: 87:14 But I, O Lord, have cried to thee: * and in the morning my prayer shall prevent thee.

segments.t: Et ego ad te, Dómine, clamávi: * et mane orátio mea prævéniet te.

content.latin: 87:15 Ut quid, Dómine, repéllis oratiónem meam: * avértis fáciem tuam a me?
content.english: 87:15 Lord, why castest thou off my prayer: * why turnest thou away thy face from me?

segments.t: Ut quid, Dómine, repéllis oratiónem meam: * avértis fáciem tuam a me?

content.latin: 87:16 Pauper sum ego, et in labóribus a iuventúte mea: * exaltátus autem, humiliátus sum et conturbátus.
content.english: 87:16 I am poor, and in labours from my youth: * and being exalted have been humbled and troubled.

segments.t: Pauper sum ego, et in labóribus a iuventúte mea: * exaltátus autem, humiliátus sum et conturbátus.

content.latin: 87:17 In me transiérunt iræ tuæ: * et terróres tui conturbavérunt me.
content.english: 87:17 Thy wrath hath come upon me: * and thy terrors have troubled me.

segments.t: In me transiérunt iræ tuæ: * et terróres tui conturbavérunt me.

content.latin: 87:18 Circumdedérunt me sicut aqua tota die: * circumdedérunt me simul.
content.english: 87:18 They have come round about me like water all the day: * they have compassed me about together.

segments.t: Circumdedérunt me sicut aqua tota die: * circumdedérunt me simul.

content.latin: 87:19 Elongásti a me amícum et próximum: * et notos meos a miséria.
content.english: 87:19 Friend and neighbour thou hast put far from me: * and my acquaintance, because of misery.

segments.t: Elongásti a me amícum et próximum: * et notos meos a miséria.

content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

segments.t: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

Psalmus 102(1-12)

content.latin: 102:1 Bénedic, ánima mea, Dómino: * et ómnia, quæ intra me sunt, nómini sancto eius.
content.english: 102:1 Bless the Lord, O my soul: * and let all that is within me bless his holy name.

segments.t: Bénedic, ánima mea, Dómino: * et ómnia, quæ intra me sunt, nómini sancto eius.

content.latin: 102:2 Bénedic, ánima mea, Dómino: * et noli oblivísci omnes retributiónes eius.
content.english: 102:2 Bless the Lord, O my soul, * and never forget all he hath done for thee.

segments.t: Bénedic, ánima mea, Dómino: * et noli oblivísci omnes retributiónes eius.

content.latin: 102:3 Qui propitiátur ómnibus iniquitátibus tuis: * qui sanat omnes infirmitátes tuas.
content.english: 102:3 Who forgiveth all thy iniquities: * who healeth all thy diseases.

segments.t: Qui propitiátur ómnibus iniquitátibus tuis: * qui sanat omnes infirmitátes tuas.

content.latin: 102:4 Qui rédimit de intéritu vitam tuam: * qui corónat te in misericórdia et miseratiónibus.
content.english: 102:4 Who redeemeth thy life from destruction: * who crowneth thee with mercy and compassion.

segments.t: Qui rédimit de intéritu vitam tuam: * qui corónat te in misericórdia et miseratiónibus.

content.latin: 102:5 Qui replet in bonis desidérium tuum: * renovábitur ut áquilæ iuvéntus tua:
content.english: 102:5 Who satisfieth thy desire with good things: * thy youth shall be renewed like the eagle’s.

segments.t: Qui replet in bonis desidérium tuum: * renovábitur ut áquilæ iuvéntus tua:

content.latin: 102:6 Fáciens misericórdias Dóminus: * et iudícium ómnibus iniúriam patiéntibus.
content.english: 102:6 The Lord doth mercies, * and judgment for all that suffer wrong.

segments.t: Fáciens misericórdias Dóminus: * et iudícium ómnibus iniúriam patiéntibus.

content.latin: 102:7 Notas fecit vias suas Móysi, * fíliis Israël voluntátes suas.
content.english: 102:7 He hath made his ways known to Moses: * his wills to the children of Israel.

segments.t: Notas fecit vias suas Móysi, * fíliis Israël voluntátes suas.

content.latin: 102:8 Miserátor, et miséricors Dóminus: * longánimis, et multum miséricors.
content.english: 102:8 The Lord is compassionate and merciful: * longsuffering and plenteous in mercy.

segments.t: Miserátor, et miséricors Dóminus: * longánimis, et multum miséricors.

content.latin: 102:9 Non in perpétuum irascétur: * neque in ætérnum comminábitur.
content.english: 102:9 He will not always be angry: * nor will he threaten for ever.

segments.t: Non in perpétuum irascétur: * neque in ætérnum comminábitur.

content.latin: 102:10 Non secúndum peccáta nostra fecit nobis: * neque secúndum iniquitátes nostras retríbuit nobis.
content.english: 102:10 He hath not dealt with us according to our sins: * nor rewarded us according to our iniquities.

segments.t: Non secúndum peccáta nostra fecit nobis: * neque secúndum iniquitátes nostras retríbuit nobis.

content.latin: 102:11 Quóniam secúndum altitúdinem cæli a terra: * corroborávit misericórdiam suam super timéntes se.
content.english: 102:11 For according to the height of the heaven above the earth: * he hath strengthened his mercy towards them that fear him.

segments.t: Quóniam secúndum altitúdinem cæli a terra: * corroborávit misericórdiam suam super timéntes se.

content.latin: 102:13 Quómodo miserétur pater filiórum, misértus est Dóminus timéntibus se: * quóniam ipse cognóvit figméntum nostrum.
content.english: 102:13 As a father hath compassion on his children, so hath the Lord compassion on them that fear him: * for he knoweth our frame.

segments.t: Quómodo miserétur pater filiórum, misértus est Dóminus timéntibus se: * quóniam ipse cognóvit figméntum nostrum.

content.latin: 102:14 Recordátus est quóniam pulvis sumus: * homo, sicut fænum dies eius, tamquam flos agri sic efflorébit.
content.english: 102:14 He remembereth that we are dust: * man’s days are as grass, as the flower of the field so shall he flourish.

segments.t: Recordátus est quóniam pulvis sumus: * homo, sicut fænum dies eius, tamquam flos agri sic efflorébit.

content.latin: 102:16 Quóniam spíritus pertransíbit in illo, et non subsístet: * et non cognóscet ámplius locum suum.
content.english: 102:16 For the spirit shall pass in him, and he shall not be: * and he shall know his place no more.

segments.t: Quóniam spíritus pertransíbit in illo, et non subsístet: * et non cognóscet ámplius locum suum.

content.latin: 102:17 Misericórdia autem Dómini ab ætérno, * et usque in ætérnum super timéntes eum.
content.english: 102:17 But the mercy of the Lord is from eternity * and unto eternity upon them that fear him:

segments.t: Misericórdia autem Dómini ab ætérno, * et usque in ætérnum super timéntes eum.

content.latin: 102:17 Et iustítia illíus in fílios filiórum, * his qui servant testaméntum eius:
content.english: 102:17 And his justice unto children’s children, * to such as keep his covenant,

segments.t: Et iustítia illíus in fílios filiórum, * his qui servant testaméntum eius:

content.latin: 102:18 Et mémores sunt mandatórum ipsíus, * ad faciéndum ea.
content.english: 102:18 And are mindful of his commandments * to do them.

segments.t: Et mémores sunt mandatórum ipsíus, * ad faciéndum ea.

content.latin: 102:19 Dóminus in cælo parávit sedem suam: * et regnum ipsíus ómnibus dominábitur.
content.english: 102:19 The Lord hath prepared his throne in heaven: * and his kingdom shall rule over all.

segments.t: Dóminus in cælo parávit sedem suam: * et regnum ipsíus ómnibus dominábitur.

content.latin: 102:20 Benedícite Dómino, omnes Ángeli eius: * poténtes virtúte, faciéntes verbum illíus, ad audiéndam vocem sermónum eius.
content.english: 102:20 Bless the Lord, all ye his angels: * you that are mighty in strength, and execute his word, hearkening to the voice of his orders.

segments.t: Benedícite Dómino, omnes Ángeli eius: * poténtes virtúte, faciéntes verbum illíus, ad audiéndam vocem sermónum eius.

content.latin: 102:21 Benedícite Dómino, omnes virtútes eius: * minístri eius, qui fácitis voluntátem eius.
content.english: 102:21 Bless the Lord, all ye his hosts: * you ministers of his that do his will.

segments.t: Benedícite Dómino, omnes virtútes eius: * minístri eius, qui fácitis voluntátem eius.

content.latin: 102:22 Benedícite Dómino, ómnia ópera eius: * in omni loco dominatiónis eius, bénedic, ánima mea, Dómino.
content.english: 102:22 Bless the Lord, all his works: * in every place of his dominion, O my soul, bless thou the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícite Dómino, ómnia ópera eius: * in omni loco dominatiónis eius, bénedic, ánima mea, Dómino.

content.latin: Vísita, quǽsumus, Dómine, habitatiónem istam, et omnes insídias inimíci ab ea longe repélle: Ángeli tui sancti hábitent in ea, qui nos in pace custódiant; et benedíctio tua sit super nos semper.
content.english: Visit, we beseech thee, O Lord, this dwelling, and drive far from it the snares of the enemy; let thy holy angels dwell herein to preserve us in peace, and let thy blessing be always upon us.

content.latin: Per Dóminum nostrum Iesum Christum, Fílium tuum: qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.
content.english: Through Jesus Christ, thy Son our Lord, Who liveth and reigneth with thee, in the unity of the Holy Ghost, God, world without end.

content.latin: Salve, Regína, mater misericórdiæ;
content.english: Hail holy Queen, Mother of Mercy,

content.latin: vita, dulcédo et spes nóstra, salve.
content.english: our life, our sweetness, and our hope.

content.latin: Ad te clamámus éxsules fílii Hevæ.
content.english: To thee do we cry, poor banished children of Eve.

content.latin: Ad te suspirámus geméntes et flentes
content.english: To thee do we send up our sighs, mourning and weeping

content.latin: In hac lacrimárum valle.
content.english: In this valley of tears.

content.latin: Eia ergo, advocáta nostra,
content.english: Turn then, most gracious Advocate,

content.latin: illos tuos misericórdes óculos ad nos convérte.
content.english: thine eyes of mercy toward us.

content.latin: Et Iesum, benedíctum fructum ventris tui,
content.english: And after this our exile show unto us

content.latin: nobis post hoc exsílium osténde.
content.english: the blessed fruit of thy womb, Jesus.

content.latin: O clemens, o pia, o dulcis Virgo María.
content.english: O clement, O loving, O sweet Virgin Mary.

content.latin: ℣. Ora pro nobis, sancta Dei Génetrix.
content.english: ℣. Pray for us, O Holy Mother of God.

segments.t: Ora pro nobis, sancta Dei Génetrix.

content.latin: ℟. Ut digni efficiámur promissiónibus Christi.
content.english: ℟. That we may be made worthy of the promises of Christ.

segments.t: Ut digni efficiámur promissiónibus Christi.

content.latin: Orémus.
content.english: Let us pray.

content.latin: Omnípotens sempitérne Deus, qui gloriósæ Vírginis Matris Maríæ corpus et ánimam, ut dignum Fílii tui habitáculum éffici mererétur, Spíritu Sancto cooperánte, præparásti: da, ut, cuius commemoratióne lætámur, eius pia intercessióne, ab instántibus malis et a morte perpétua liberémur. Per eúndem Christum Dóminum nostrum. Amen.
content.english: O almighty, everlasting God, who by the cooperation of the Holy Spirit, didst prepare the body and soul of Mary, glorious Virgin and Mother, to become a worthy dwelling for Thy Son; grant that we who rejoice in her commemoration may, by her gracious intercession, be delivered from present evils and from everlasting death. Through the same Christ our Lord. Amen.

content.latin: ℣. Divínum auxílium ✠ máneat semper nobíscum.
content.english: ℣. May the divine assistance ✠ remain with us always.

segments.t: Divínum auxílium ✠ máneat semper nobíscum.

content.english: ℟. Amen.
